issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Rideable.messageOnRide() as a no-argument method returning String, and the provided template Main.java calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments. However, the solution implementation defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) (i.e., it takes a parameter) and the implementing classes (Pig, Seal) implement messageOnRide(String). This parameter mismatch prevents students from following the specification and from compiling/calling the method as shown in the template Main.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts: change Rideable.messageOnRide to a no-argument method (String messageOnRide()), and update Pig and Seal to implement the no-arg version returning the expected string (e.g., "Riding on Pig Doodle"). Alternatively, if an equipment parameter is intentional, update the problem statement UML and the template Main (calls) to use the parameter consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument Rideable.messageOnRide() that returns "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (see UML and Main usage), but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and has implementations in Pig and Seal that require an equipment parameter. This signature/name mismatch breaks the conceptual mapping (e.g., template's Main calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments) and forces students to reconcile conflicting APIs across artifacts.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent by changing the solution to match the problem/template: update Rideable to declare messageOnRide() with no parameters and change Pig and Seal implementations to override messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". (Alternatively, if an equipment parameter is intended, update the problem statement and template Main usage to require messageOnRide(String equipment) and show its use.)
